The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
__part_stat_add(part, io_ticks, 1);
```
```c
update_io_ticks(part, jiffies);
```
```c
update_io_ticks(part, now);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `io_ticks` is only incremented by 1 for each I/O request, regardless of its duration. This means that for requests lasting longer than two jiffies, only the first and last jiffies are counted, leading to an inaccurate approximation of the actual I/O time, especially for slow disks that process requests sequentially.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
__part_stat_add(part, io_ticks, end ? now - stamp : 1);
```
```c
update_io_ticks(part, jiffies, false);
```
```c
update_io_ticks(part, now, true);
```
Reason:
The fix modifies the `update_io_ticks` function to account for the actual time elapsed between updates by using `now - stamp` when the request ends, rather than just adding 1. This ensures that the total I/O time is accurately reflected in `io_ticks`, thus providing a more precise measurement of I/O activity for slow disks.
